wins.text: FEC adjusted operating income increased $168M, up 17% YoY with adjusted operating margin expanding 70 bps — fourth consecutive quarter of YoY adjusted margin expansion
Consolidated adjusted EPS of $3.83, up 6% YoY, above the midpoint of Q1 outlook range despite $150M international export headwind and $130M USPS contract expiration headwind
U.S. domestic ADV grew 5% YoY with U.S. domestic package yield up 3%; Best Buy named FedEx as primary national parcel carrier; U.S. domestic small business revenue grew more than 10% YoY
International priority and economy freight revenue grew 14% YoY with high flow-through, driven by Tricolor capacity pivot from Asia-U.S. to Asia-Europe lanes
Repurchased $500M of stock in Q1; $1.6B remaining under 2024 authorization; quarterly dividend increased; euro-denominated bond offering significantly oversubscribed

risks.text: $1 billion full-year headwind to adjusted operating income from global trade environment, including de minimis exemption removal, reduced China-to-U.S. demand, $300M in direct trade-related expenses (customs clearance, staffing), and $160M USPS contract expiration headwind

FedEx Freight adjusted operating income declined ~$70M with adjusted operating margin contracting 250 bps; LTL market weakness from industrial economy softness and excess truckload capacity continues to pressure results

Full-year adjusted EPS range of $17.20–$19.00 is wide ($1.80 spread), reflecting significant uncertainty around global trade evolution, industrial economy health, and U.S. domestic demand trajectory in H2
International export volumes declined materially on China-to-U.S. lane due to de minimis exemption changes; $150M OI headwind in Q1 alone expected to intensify to ~$1B for full year
Higher-than-expected Q1 GAAP tax rate of 27.3% due to nonrecurring income tax expense from examination of prior year tax return filings; FY26 effective tax rate guided at ~25%

guidance_items.detail: FY26 adjusted EPS guided at $17.20–$19.00; midpoint $18.10 assumes 5% consolidated revenue growth and $1B in transformation savings; no prior full-year EPS guidance had been issued publicly on this call, but range introduced here
FY26 consolidated revenue growth guided at 4%–6%; FEC revenue expected up ~6% at midpoint; FedEx Freight revenue expected flat to up modestly YoY
FEC adjusted operating margin expected down slightly at midpoint; FedEx Freight margin expected down YoY at midpoint
FY26 CapEx target maintained at $4.5B; Q1 CapEx was $623M
Voluntary pension cash contributions reduced to up to $400M from prior forecast of up to $600M for FY26

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: Why operating leverage is not materializing despite 5% revenue growth and $1B cost savings — analysts pressed repeatedly on the flow-through gap
Specific composition and magnitude of the $1B global trade headwind broken down by revenue loss vs. direct cost increases (not proactively disaggregated in prepared remarks)
Competitive landscape dynamics and UPS market share contraction creating share gain opportunities for FedEx domestic parcel
